															BTSC Staff Nurse Recruitment 2025 Exam Pattern 

															1. Selection Process: The selection of candidates will be based on the merit list prepared on the basis of the marks obtained in the online computer-based competitive examination and experience.

															(i) Merit List Preparation for Selection: The merit list for selection will be prepared in the following manner:

															(a) Online Computer Based Test: 75 Marks * Full marks for the online computer-based examination will be 75. The question paper will be of objective type (multiple choice).

															(b) Marks for Experience in Government Hospitals/Government Institutions/Government Schemes/Health Institutions run by Government-aided Societies/Registered Private Hospitals: 25 Marks * For experience in the aforementioned institutions, a maximum of 25 marks will be awarded. For each completed year of experience, 05 marks will be given. Fractions of a year will not be considered.

															Total Marks: 100 Marks

															Note:

															(i) It will be mandatory for candidates to obtain minimum qualifying marks in the online computer-based examination. The minimum qualifying marks will be 40% for unreserved category, 36.5% for backward class, 34% for extremely backward class, and 32% for Scheduled Castes/Scheduled Tribes/Women/Persons with Disabilities (Divyang).

															(ii) The online computer-based examination will be conducted for all eligible candidates.

															(ii) Examination Scheme:

															(a) The question paper for the competitive examination will consist of a total of 100 questions. All questions will be of objective (multiple choice) type.

															(b) The duration of the examination will be two hours, and the total marks will be 100.

															(c) The syllabus for the examination will be based on the prescribed curriculum for General Nursing and Midwifery (G.N.M.). Detailed syllabus will be published separately on the website of the Commission.

															(d) The online computer-based examination may be conducted in multiple shifts. Due to this, the method of normalization of marks will be adopted to ensure fairness in the evaluation of results. Candidates will have to prepare themselves accordingly.

															(e) There will be negative marking for incorrect answers in the examination. For each incorrect answer, 0.25 marks will be deducted.

															(f) The process of normalization of marks will be adopted for all candidates appearing in the examination.

															(g) Regarding the relaxation in the qualifying marks for extremely backward class and backward class, as per the Department of Health, Government of Bihar's letter no.-2374, dated 16.07.2007, and General Administration Department, Bihar's letter no.-962, dated 22.01.2021, the minimum qualifying marks in the written examination will be 40% for unreserved category, 36.5% for backward class, 34% for extremely backward class, and 32% for Scheduled Castes/Scheduled Tribes, women, and persons with disabilities (Divyang).

															Note: Candidates who do not obtain the prescribed minimum qualifying marks in the competitive examination will not be included in any merit list.

															(iv) The format for the experience certificate is attached as Annexure-1. Only experience certificates issued in this format will be considered for awarding marks for experience and age relaxation. Experience certificates issued in any other format will not be eligible for marks or age relaxation.

															(v) As per the rules, candidates who qualify in the written competitive examination will be invited for document verification based on the category-wise merit list prepared according to the provisions mentioned in Clause-5(i) of the advertisement.

															BTSC Staff Nurse Recruitment 2025 Exam Pattern 

															1. Selection Process: The selection of candidates will be based on the merit list prepared on the basis of the marks obtained in the online computer-based competitive examination and experience.

															(i) Merit List Preparation for Selection: The merit list for selection will be prepared in the following manner:

															(a) Online Computer Based Test: 75 Marks * Full marks for the online computer-based examination will be 75. The question paper will be of objective type (multiple choice).

															(b) Marks for Experience in Government Hospitals/Government Institutions/Government Schemes/Health Institutions run by Government-aided Societies/Registered Private Hospitals: 25 Marks * For experience in the aforementioned institutions, a maximum of 25 marks will be awarded. For each completed year of experience, 05 marks will be given. Fractions of a year will not be considered.

															Total Marks: 100 Marks

															Note:

															(i) It will be mandatory for candidates to obtain minimum qualifying marks in the online computer-based examination. The minimum qualifying marks will be 40% for unreserved category, 36.5% for backward class, 34% for extremely backward class, and 32% for Scheduled Castes/Scheduled Tribes/Women/Persons with Disabilities (Divyang).

															(ii) The online computer-based examination will be conducted for all eligible candidates.

															(ii) Examination Scheme:

															(a) The question paper for the competitive examination will consist of a total of 100 questions. All questions will be of objective (multiple choice) type.

															(b) The duration of the examination will be two hours, and the total marks will be 100.

															(c) The syllabus for the examination will be based on the prescribed curriculum for General Nursing and Midwifery (G.N.M.). Detailed syllabus will be published separately on the website of the Commission.

															(d) The online computer-based examination may be conducted in multiple shifts. Due to this, the method of normalization of marks will be adopted to ensure fairness in the evaluation of results. Candidates will have to prepare themselves accordingly.

															(e) There will be negative marking for incorrect answers in the examination. For each incorrect answer, 0.25 marks will be deducted.

															(f) The process of normalization of marks will be adopted for all candidates appearing in the examination.

															(g) Regarding the relaxation in the qualifying marks for extremely backward class and backward class, as per the Department of Health, Government of Bihar's letter no.-2374, dated 16.07.2007, and General Administration Department, Bihar's letter no.-962, dated 22.01.2021, the minimum qualifying marks in the written examination will be 40% for unreserved category, 36.5% for backward class, 34% for extremely backward class, and 32% for Scheduled Castes/Scheduled Tribes, women, and persons with disabilities (Divyang).

															Note: Candidates who do not obtain the prescribed minimum qualifying marks in the competitive examination will not be included in any merit list.

															(iv) The format for the experience certificate is attached as Annexure-1. Only experience certificates issued in this format will be considered for awarding marks for experience and age relaxation. Experience certificates issued in any other format will not be eligible for marks or age relaxation.

															(v) As per the rules, candidates who qualify in the written competitive examination will be invited for document verification based on the category-wise merit list prepared according to the provisions mentioned in Clause-5(i) of the advertisement.

				Mental Ability, Statistics (Secondary Level), Mathematics (Secondary Level), Language Ability (Hindi & English)

				General Science, Indian Polity, Geography of Rajasthan

			Duration: 3 hours
			Subjects Covered:

			
				
				Subject Knowledge (Senior Secondary Level)

				Subject Knowledge (Post-Graduation Level)
				
				
				Pedagogy, Teaching Learning Material, ICT in Teaching & Learning
				
			

			 

			🏆 Scheme for the post of Coach

			Maximum Marks: 200

				History of Rajasthan & Indian History (with emphasis on Indian National Movement)
				
				
				Mental Ability, Maths (Secondary Level), Statistics (Secondary Level), Language Ability (Hindi, English)
				
				
				Current Affairs
				
				
				General Science, Indian Polity, Geography of Rajasthan

			Duration: 3 Hours
			Maximum Marks: 260

			Subjects Covered:

			
				
				Knowledge of Physical Education & Sports
				
				
				Sports Sciences

				Pedagogy, Teaching Learning Material, ICT in Teaching & Learning

			RRB NTPC 10+2 Level Recruitment 2025 Exam Pattern / Syllabus

			Exam Pattern

			**1. Computer-Based Test (CBT) Stage 1:

			
				
				Type: Objective Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs)
				
				Duration: 90 minutes
				Number of Questions: 100
				Sections:
				
					General Awareness
					Mathematics
					General Intelligence and Reasoning
				
				
				Marking Scheme:
				
					General Awareness: 40 Questions
					Mathematics: 30 Questions
					General Intelligence and Reasoning: 30 Questions
					Total Marks: 100
					Negative Marking: 1/3 mark will be deducted for each wrong answer.
				
				
			

			**2. Computer-Based Test (CBT) Stage 2:

			
				Type: Objective Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs)
				Duration: 90 minutes
				Number of Questions: 120
				Sections:
				
					General Awareness
					Mathematics
					General Intelligence and Reasoning
					Specific to Post (subject-specific questions)
				
				
				Marking Scheme:
				
					General Awareness: 50 Questions
					Mathematics: 35 Questions
					General Intelligence and Reasoning: 35 Questions
					Total Marks: 120
					Negative Marking: 1/3 mark will be deducted for each wrong answer.
				
				
			

			**3. Skill Test (if applicable):

			
				Type: Depending on the post, this may include typing tests, computer-based tests, or other specific skill assessments.
			

			**4. Document Verification:

			
				Candidates who clear the CBT and Skill Test (if applicable) will undergo document verification to validate their eligibility and credentials.
			

			Syllabus

			**1. General Awareness:

			
				Current Affairs (National and International)
				Indian History and Culture
				Geography
				Indian Polity and Constitution
				Economy
				General Science
				Environmental Issues
			

			**2. Mathematics:

			
				Number Systems
				Algebra
				Geometry
				Trigonometry
				Mensuration
				Arithmetic (Percentage, Profit and Loss, Simple and Compound Interest, Ratio and Proportion)
			

			**3. General Intelligence and Reasoning:

			
				Analogies
				Blood Relations
				Coding-Decoding
				Syllogism
				Direction Sense
				Decision Making
				Non-Verbal Reasoning (Series, Patterns)
			

			**4. Post-Specific Syllabus (for Stage 2):

			
				Depending on the specific NTPC post applied for, there might be additional subject-specific questions in CBT Stage 2. This could include questions related to the job profile and technical skills relevant to the position.
			

			Preparation Tips:

			
				Study Regularly: Follow a structured study plan covering all sections.
				Practice Mock Tests: Familiarize yourself with the exam format and time management.
				Stay Updated: Read newspapers and current affairs magazines to enhance your General Awareness.
				Review Previous Papers: Practice previous years' question papers to understand the exam pattern and question types.

			**1. Computer-Based Test (CBT) Stage 1:

					General Awareness

					Mathematics: 30 Questions

					Total Marks: 100
					Negative Marking: 1/3 mark will be deducted for each wrong answer.
				
				
			

			**2. Computer-Based Test (CBT) Stage 2:

			
				Type: Objective Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs)
				Duration: 90 minutes
				Number of Questions: 120
				Sections:
				
					General Awareness
					Mathematics
					General Intelligence and Reasoning
					Specific to Post (subject-specific questions)
				
				
				Marking Scheme:
				
					General Awareness: 50 Questions
					Mathematics: 35 Questions
					General Intelligence and Reasoning: 35 Questions
					Total Marks: 120
					Negative Marking: 1/3 mark will be deducted for each wrong answer.
				
				
			

			**3. Skill Test (if applicable):

			
				Type: Depending on the post, this may include typing tests, computer-based tests, or other specific skill assessments.
			

			**4. Document Verification:

			
				Candidates who clear the CBT and Skill Test (if applicable) will undergo document verification to validate their eligibility and credentials.
			

			Syllabus

			**1. General Awareness:

			
				Current Affairs (National and International)
				Indian History and Culture
				Geography
				Indian Polity and Constitution
				Economy
				General Science
				Environmental Issues
			

			**2. Mathematics:

			
				Number Systems
				Algebra
				Geometry
				Trigonometry
				Mensuration
				Arithmetic (Percentage, Profit and Loss, Simple and Compound Interest, Ratio and Proportion)
			

			**3. General Intelligence and Reasoning:

			
				Analogies
				Blood Relations
				Coding-Decoding
				Syllogism
				Direction Sense
				Decision Making
				Non-Verbal Reasoning (Series, Patterns)
			

			**4. Post-Specific Syllabus (for Stage 2):

			
				Depending on the specific NTPC post applied for, there might be additional subject-specific questions in CBT Stage 2. This could include questions related to the job profile and technical skills relevant to the position.

General Knowledge (SEO Friendly)


    The General Knowledge syllabus for the written examination includes a wide range of important topics 
    such as General Knowledge, General Science, Indian History, Indian Constitution, Indian Economy, 
    Indian Culture, Agriculture, Commerce and Trade, Population Studies, Environment and Urbanization. 
    Candidates must also prepare Geography of India, Natural Resources of Uttar Pradesh, specific 
    information related to Education, Culture and Social Traditions of UP, major fairs and festivals 
    organized in the state, and achievements in Sports.



    The syllabus further covers Revenue and Police Administration in UP, Human Rights, Internal Security 
    and Terrorism, India’s Relations with Neighbouring Countries, contemporary issues of National and 
    International importance, and details of National and International Organizations. Topics such as 
    Awards and Recognition, Countries–Capitals–Currencies, Important Days, Inventions and Discoveries, 
    Famous Books and their Writers, and Social Media Communication are also included.



    Candidates should also focus on Government welfare schemes of Uttar Pradesh, Women Empowerment 
    initiatives, Self-Reliance and Industrial Development Programs, Natural Phenomena, and Important 
    Summits. This comprehensive syllabus plays a crucial role in enhancing general awareness and helps 
    aspirants score well in the examination.

General Knowledge (SEO Friendly)


    The General Knowledge syllabus for the written examination includes a wide range of important topics 
    such as General Knowledge, General Science, Indian History, Indian Constitution, Indian Economy, 
    Indian Culture, Agriculture, Commerce and Trade, Population Studies, Environment and Urbanization. 
    Candidates must also prepare Geography of India, Natural Resources of Uttar Pradesh, specific 
    information related to Education, Culture and Social Traditions of UP, major fairs and festivals 
    organized in the state, and achievements in Sports.



    The syllabus further covers Revenue and Police Administration in UP, Human Rights, Internal Security 
    and Terrorism, India’s Relations with Neighbouring Countries, contemporary issues of National and 
    International importance, and details of National and International Organizations. Topics such as 
    Awards and Recognition, Countries–Capitals–Currencies, Important Days, Inventions and Discoveries, 
    Famous Books and their Writers, and Social Media Communication are also included.



    Candidates should also focus on Government welfare schemes of Uttar Pradesh, Women Empowerment 
    initiatives, Self-Reliance and Industrial Development Programs, Natural Phenomena, and Important 
    Summits. This comprehensive syllabus plays a crucial role in enhancing general awareness and helps 
    aspirants score well in the examination.

															RRB NTPC Recruitment 2024 Exam Pattern / Syllabus

															

															Exam Pattern

															**1. Computer-Based Test (CBT) Stage 1:

															
																Type: Objective Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs)
																Duration: 90 minutes
																Number of Questions: 100
																Sections:
																
																	General Awareness
																	Mathematics
																	General Intelligence and Reasoning
																
																
																Marking Scheme:
																
																	General Awareness: 40 Questions
																	Mathematics: 30 Questions
																	General Intelligence and Reasoning: 30 Questions
																	Total Marks: 100
																	Negative Marking: 1/3 mark will be deducted for each wrong answer.
																
																
															

															**2. Computer-Based Test (CBT) Stage 2:

															
																Type: Objective Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs)
																Duration: 90 minutes
																Number of Questions: 120
																Sections:
																
																	General Awareness
																	Mathematics
																	General Intelligence and Reasoning
																	Specific to Post (subject-specific questions)
																
																
																Marking Scheme:
																
																	General Awareness: 50 Questions
																	Mathematics: 35 Questions
																	General Intelligence and Reasoning: 35 Questions
																	Total Marks: 120
																	Negative Marking: 1/3 mark will be deducted for each wrong answer.
																
																
															

															**3. Skill Test (if applicable):

															
																Type: Depending on the post, this may include typing tests, computer-based tests, or other specific skill assessments.
															

															**4. Document Verification:

															
																Candidates who clear the CBT and Skill Test (if applicable) will undergo document verification to validate their eligibility and credentials.
															

															Syllabus

															**1. General Awareness:

															
																Current Affairs (National and International)
																Indian History and Culture
																Geography
																Indian Polity and Constitution
																Economy
																General Science
																Environmental Issues
															

															**2. Mathematics:

															
																Number Systems
																Algebra
																Geometry
																Trigonometry
																Mensuration
																Arithmetic (Percentage, Profit and Loss, Simple and Compound Interest, Ratio and Proportion)
															

															**3. General Intelligence and Reasoning:

															
																Analogies
																Blood Relations
																Coding-Decoding
																Syllogism
																Direction Sense
																Decision Making
																Non-Verbal Reasoning (Series, Patterns)
															

															**4. Post-Specific Syllabus (for Stage 2):

															
																Depending on the specific NTPC post applied for, there might be additional subject-specific questions in CBT Stage 2. This could include questions related to the job profile and technical skills relevant to the position.
															

															Preparation Tips:

															
																Study Regularly: Follow a structured study plan covering all sections.
																Practice Mock Tests: Familiarize yourself with the exam format and time management.
																Stay Updated: Read newspapers and current affairs magazines to enhance your General Awareness.
																Review Previous Papers: Practice previous years' question papers to understand the exam pattern and question types.

															RRB NTPC Recruitment 2024 Exam Pattern / Syllabus

															

															Exam Pattern

															**1. Computer-Based Test (CBT) Stage 1:

															
																Type: Objective Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs)
																Duration: 90 minutes
																Number of Questions: 100
																Sections:
																
																	General Awareness
																	Mathematics
																	General Intelligence and Reasoning
																
																
																Marking Scheme:
																
																	General Awareness: 40 Questions
																	Mathematics: 30 Questions
																	General Intelligence and Reasoning: 30 Questions
																	Total Marks: 100
																	Negative Marking: 1/3 mark will be deducted for each wrong answer.
																
																
															

															**2. Computer-Based Test (CBT) Stage 2:

															
																Type: Objective Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs)
																Duration: 90 minutes
																Number of Questions: 120
																Sections:
																
																	General Awareness
																	Mathematics
																	General Intelligence and Reasoning
																	Specific to Post (subject-specific questions)
																
																
																Marking Scheme:
																
																	General Awareness: 50 Questions
																	Mathematics: 35 Questions
																	General Intelligence and Reasoning: 35 Questions
																	Total Marks: 120
																	Negative Marking: 1/3 mark will be deducted for each wrong answer.
																
																
															

															**3. Skill Test (if applicable):

															
																Type: Depending on the post, this may include typing tests, computer-based tests, or other specific skill assessments.
															

															**4. Document Verification:

															
																Candidates who clear the CBT and Skill Test (if applicable) will undergo document verification to validate their eligibility and credentials.
															

															Syllabus

															**1. General Awareness:

															
																Current Affairs (National and International)
																Indian History and Culture
																Geography
																Indian Polity and Constitution
																Economy
																General Science
																Environmental Issues
															

															**2. Mathematics:

															
																Number Systems
																Algebra
																Geometry
																Trigonometry
																Mensuration
																Arithmetic (Percentage, Profit and Loss, Simple and Compound Interest, Ratio and Proportion)
															

															**3. General Intelligence and Reasoning:

															
																Analogies
																Blood Relations
																Coding-Decoding
																Syllogism
																Direction Sense
																Decision Making
																Non-Verbal Reasoning (Series, Patterns)
															

															**4. Post-Specific Syllabus (for Stage 2):

															
																Depending on the specific NTPC post applied for, there might be additional subject-specific questions in CBT Stage 2. This could include questions related to the job profile and technical skills relevant to the position.
															

															Preparation Tips:

															
																Study Regularly: Follow a structured study plan covering all sections.
																Practice Mock Tests: Familiarize yourself with the exam format and time management.
																Stay Updated: Read newspapers and current affairs magazines to enhance your General Awareness.
																Review Previous Papers: Practice previous years' question papers to understand the exam pattern and question types.

															BOB LBO 2026: Required Documents for Upload

															
																Resume (PDF)
																Date of Birth Proof: 10th marksheet/certificate (PDF)
																Educational Certificates: Relevant Mark-Sheets/Certificate (PDF). Please scan ALL your educational certificates into a single PDF file.
																Work Experience Certificates (PDF) (if applicable)
																Caste/Category Certificate (PDF) (if applicable)
																PWD (Persons with Disability) Certificate (PDF) (if applicable)

															Important Specifications for Uploading:

															Before applying online, make sure you have scanned (digital) images of all the above documents according to these specifications:

															
																Format: All documents must be in PDF format.
																Page Size: The document page size should be A4.
																File Size Limit: The size of each PDF file should not exceed 500 KB.
																Scanning Tips: If you are scanning documents, ensure they are saved as PDFs and their size is not more than 500 KB. If a file is larger than 500 KB, adjust your scanner settings (like DPI resolution, number of colors, etc.) during the scanning process to reduce the file size.
																Clarity: Please ensure that all uploaded documents are clear and readable.
															

															How to Capture Your Live Photo:

															You will need to capture and upload a live photograph using either a webcam or your mobile phone.

															
																
																Using a Webcam:

																
																	
																	Select the "Capture Photo" option.
																	
																	
																	Your webcam will turn on, allowing you to take your picture.
																	
																	
																	The picture will automatically be uploaded to your application form.
																	
																
																
																
																Using a Mobile Phone:

																
																	
																	Select the "Click here to Scan" option.
																	
																	
																	Scan the QR code displayed on your screen with your mobile phone.
																	
																	
																	This will open a website on your phone, where you can take your picture.
																	
																	
																	After taking the picture and selecting it, it will automatically be uploaded to your application form.
																	
																
																
															

															Do's and Don'ts for Photo Capture:

															Do's:

															
																
																Make sure your photo is taken against a light-colored, preferably white background, with good lighting.
																
																
																Look straight at the webcam/camera.
																
																
																The photograph should be passport-sized.
																
															

															Don'ts:

															
																
																Do not click or upload a small-sized photograph.
																
																
																Do not wear colored glasses, sunglasses, or a cap.
																
																
																Avoid shadows on your face, not facing the camera, a distorted face, a face covered with a mask, or a blurred image.
																
																
																Do not take the photo in a dark or improper background.

																The photograph should be passport-sized.
																
															

															Don'ts:

																Do not wear colored glasses, sunglasses, or a cap.

															BPSC TRE 4.0 Post Wise Education Qualification
															
														
														
															
															School Teacher

															(Class 1 to 5)
															
															
															
															
																
																General Eligibility: Senior Secondary (10+2) with at least 50% marks and a 2-year Diploma in Elementary Education (D.El.Ed) OR Senior Secondary with 45% marks and 2-year D.El.Ed as per NCTE Regulations 2002 OR Senior Secondary with 50% marks and 4-year B.El.Ed OR Graduation with 2-year D.El.Ed.
																
																
																Urdu Teacher: Maulvi/Alim from Bihar State Madarsa Education Board/MMHAPU Patna, or Intermediate in Urdu (minimum 50 marks), or Graduation in Urdu.
																
																
																Bangla Teacher: Intermediate with Bangla (minimum 50 marks) or Graduation in Bangla.
																
																
																NIOS D.El.Ed Note: 18-month NIOS D.El.Ed diploma is valid only for teachers appointed and working before August 10, 2017.
																
																
																Form More Details, Read Official Notification. 
																
															
															
															
														
														
															
															Middle School Teacher (Class 6 to 8)
															
															
															
																
																General Eligibility: Graduation Degree with 2-year D.El.Ed OR Graduation / Post Graduation with minimum 50% marks and B.Ed OR Graduation with 45% marks and 1-year B.Ed (NCTE norms) OR Senior Secondary with 50% marks and 4-year B.El.Ed / B.A.Ed / B.Sc.Ed OR Graduation/PG with 55% marks and 3-year Integrated B.Ed-M.Ed.
																
																
																Technical / Specific Degree Eligibility: BCA + D.El.Ed/B.Ed, MCA + 3-year Integrated B.Ed-M.Ed, B.Tech (Science & Math specialization) + B.Ed, or B.Sc (Bio-Technology / Electronics) + B.Ed.
																
																
																Subject Group Criteria:

																
																	
																	Language: Studied the concerned language at the Graduation level as Honours/Subsidiary (e.g., Shastri/Graduation for Sanskrit, Alim/Graduation for Urdu).
																	
																	
																	Social Science: Studied any two subjects at Graduation level among History, Geography, Political Science, Philosophy, Economics, Commerce, Psychology, Sociology, Home Science.
																	
																	
																	Math & Science: Studied any two subjects at Graduation level among Mathematics, Statistics, Physics, Chemistry, Zoology, Botany.
																	
																
																
																Form More Details, Read Official Notification. 
															
															
														
														
															
															Secondary School Teacher (General Subject) (Class 9 to 10)
															
															
															
																Graduation / Post Graduation in the concerned subject with minimum 50% marks + B.Ed (OR 45% marks as per NCTE 2002/2007 norms + B.Ed) OR 4-Year Integrated B.A.Ed / B.Sc.Ed.
																Form More Details, Read Official Notification. 
															
															
														
														
															Physical EducationTeacher (TGT) (Class 9 to 10)
															
															
																Bachelor's Degree in Physical Education with minimum 50% marks OR Graduation with 45% marks and participation in National/Inter-University sports/games OR 3-Year B.P.Ed degree or equivalent.
																Form More Details, Read Official Notification. 
															
															
														
														
															Secondary School Teacher (Class 9 to 10)
															
															
																
																Music (Code E): Graduation Degree in Music with minimum 50% marks from a recognized University/Board.
																
																
																Fine Arts (Code F): Graduation Degree in Fine Arts with minimum 50% marks from a recognized University/Board.
																
																
																Dance (Code G): Graduation Degree in Dance Education with minimum 50% marks from a recognized University/Board.
																
																
																Mathematics Subject Group: Studied Mathematics with any two subjects among Physics, Electronics, Computer Science, Chemistry, or Statistics at the Graduation level OR B.E./B.Tech degree with specialization in Mathematics (BCA included).
																
																
																Science Subject Group: Studied Zoology, Botany, and Chemistry at the Graduation level OR B.E./B.Tech degree with specialization in Science (Includes Biotechnology & Microbiology).
																
																
																Social Science Subject Group: Passed any two subjects at the Graduation level among History, Geography, Economics, and Political Science (History or Geography is mandatory). Ancient History is considered equivalent to History.
																
																
																Languages: Studied the concerned language as an Honours/Subsidiary subject at the Graduation level.
																
																
																Form More Details, Read Official Notification. 
																
															
															
														
														
															
															Secondary School Teacher (TGT)-Special (Class 9 to 10)
															
															
															
																Graduation Degree with minimum 50% marks + B.Ed in Special Education (with valid CRR No. registered with RCI) + 6-month Training in Cross Disability (If training is not completed, 2-year timeline allowed post-appointment).
																Form More Details, Read Official Notification. 
															
															
														
														
															
															10+2 School Teacher (PGT) (Class 11 to 12)
															
															
															
																
																General Subjects: Post Graduation (Master's Degree) in the concerned subject with minimum 50% marks + B.Ed (OR 45% marks as per NCTE 2002/2007 norms) OR BA.Ed / B.Sc.Ed OR Minimum 55% marks in PG with 3-Year Integrated B.Ed-M.Ed.
																
																
																Computer Science (Code L): B.E/B.Tech (CS/IT), MCA, M.Sc (CS), B.Sc (CS)/BCA with PG degree, or DOEACC 'A'/'B'/'C' Level with PG/Graduation. (B.Ed is not mandatory for Computer Science).
																
																
																Music (Code M): Master's Degree (M.Mus) in Music Education with minimum 50% marks.
																
																
																Commerce (Code N): M.Com in Commerce (EPS, Accountancy, or Business Studies). (M.Com in Applied/Business Economics is not eligible).
																
																
																Agriculture (Code O): Graduation in Agriculture/Horticulture with 50% marks + Master's Degree in Agronomy, Plant Breeding & Genetics, Entomology, Plant Pathology, Seed Science, Soil Science, or Horticulture.
																
																Form More Details, Read Official Notification. 
															
															
														
														
															
															Important Key Guidelines:

															
																
																Age & Reservation Relaxation: Minimum qualifying marks relaxed by 5% for SC, ST, EBC, BC, and PwD candidates in essential educational eligibility.
																
																
																Equivalent Qualifications: Fazil degree is recognized as equivalent to PG, and Alim / Shastri degrees are recognized as equivalent to Graduation for concerned language subjects.

																Bangla Teacher: Intermediate with Bangla (minimum 50 marks) or Graduation in Bangla.

															Middle School Teacher (Class 6 to 8)
															
															
															
																
																General Eligibility: Graduation Degree with 2-year D.El.Ed OR Graduation / Post Graduation with minimum 50% marks and B.Ed OR Graduation with 45% marks and 1-year B.Ed (NCTE norms) OR Senior Secondary with 50% marks and 4-year B.El.Ed / B.A.Ed / B.Sc.Ed OR Graduation/PG with 55% marks and 3-year Integrated B.Ed-M.Ed.
																
																
																Technical / Specific Degree Eligibility: BCA + D.El.Ed/B.Ed, MCA + 3-year Integrated B.Ed-M.Ed, B.Tech (Science & Math specialization) + B.Ed, or B.Sc (Bio-Technology / Electronics) + B.Ed.
																
																
																Subject Group Criteria:

																	Social Science: Studied any two subjects at Graduation level among History, Geography, Political Science, Philosophy, Economics, Commerce, Psychology, Sociology, Home Science.

															Eligibility Code for NTA NEET 2026
															
														
														
															
															 

															
																NEET UG Code 01: A candidate who is appearing in the qualifying examination, i.e., 12 Standard in 2021 whose result is awaited may apply and take up the said test but he/she shall not be eligible for admission to the MBBS or BDS, if he/she does not pass the qualifying examination with the required pass percentage of marks at the time of first round of Counseling.
															

															 

															
																NEET UG Code 02 : The Higher/Senior Secondary Examination or the Indian School Certificate Examination which is equivalent to 10+2 Higher/Senior Secondary Examination after a period of 12 years study, the last two years of such study comprising of Physics, Chemistry, Biology/Bio-technology (which shall include practical tests in these subjects) and Mathematics or any other elective subject with English at a level not less than the core course for English as prescribed by the National Council of Educational Research and Training after introduction of the 10+2+3 educational structure as recommended by the National Committee on Education.
															

															 

															
																NEET UG Code 03 : The Intermediate/Pre-degree Examination in Science of an Indian University/Board or other recognized examining body with Physics, Chemistry, Biology /Bio-technology (which shall include practical test in these subjects) and also English as a compulsory subject
															

															 

															
																NEET UG Code 04 : The Pre-professional/Pre-medical Examination with Physics ,Chemistry, Biology/Bio-technology & English after passing either the Higher Secondary Examination or the Pre-University or an equivalent examination. The Pre-professional/Pre-medical examination shall include practical test in these subjects and also English as a compulsory subject.
															

															 

															
																NEET UG Code 05 : The first year of the three years’ degree course of a recognized University with Physics, Chemistry and Biology/Bio-technology including practical tests in these subjects provided the examination is a University Examination and candidate has passed the earlier qualifying examination with Physics, Chemistry, Biology/Bio-Technology with English at a level not less than a core course.
															

															 

															
																NEET UG Code 06 : B.Sc.Examination of an Indian University provided that he/she has passed the B.Sc.Examination with not less than two of the subjects Physics, Chemistry, Biology (Botany, Zoology)/Bio-technology and further that he/she has passed the earlier qualifying examination with Physics,Chemistry,Biology and English.
															

															 

															
																NEET UG Code 07: Any other examination which in scope and standard (Last 02 years of 10+2 Study comprising of Physics, Chemistry and Biology/ Bio-technology; which shall include practical test in these  subjects) is found to be equivalent to the Intermediate Science Examination of an Indian University/ Board, taking Physics, Chemistry and Biology/Biotechnology including practical tests in each of these subjects and English
